common cold.vaccine_schedule: No vaccine available; symptomatic management recommended.
myths: Cold exposure causes cold - False
common cold.outbreak_info: No active outbreak reported in dataset.
treatment: There is no cure; it usually clears on its own in about a week
Rest and drink plenty of warm fluids
Gargle with warm salt water for a sore throat
Paracetamol can ease fever and aches as per label or doctor's advice
Antibiotics do not work on colds
See a doctor if symptoms last more than 10 days or breathing becomes difficult

myths: All fevers indicate serious disease - False
headache.outbreak_info: No active outbreak reported in dataset.
treatment: Rest in a quiet, dim room and drink water
A cold or warm compress on the head or neck can help
Paracetamol can be used as per label or doctor's advice
Get urgent care for a sudden, very severe headache, or one with stiff neck, confusion, weakness, vision loss or after a head injury

myths: Only elderly get heart attacks - False
treatment: This is a medical emergency: call the emergency number or go to a hospital immediately
Do not drive yourself; sit down and stay calm
Emergency staff may advise chewing an aspirin if you are not allergic
Hospital treatment includes clot-dissolving medicines or opening the blocked artery with a procedure
Quick treatment saves heart muscle and lives

myths: Eating sugar directly causes diabetes - False
treatment: Diabetes cannot usually be cured but can be well controlled
Follow a balanced diet, stay active and keep a healthy weight
Take medicines or insulin exactly as prescribed by a doctor
Check blood sugar regularly and attend regular checkups
Some people with type 2 diabetes can reach remission through weight loss, with medical guidance

myths: All cancers are fatal - False
Injuries cause cancer - False
treatment: Treatment depends on the type and stage of cancer
Options include surgery, chemotherapy, radiation, targeted therapy and immunotherapy
Many cancers can be cured or controlled when found early
See a doctor or cancer specialist quickly if you notice a lump or unexplained weight loss

myths: Non-smokers cannot get lung diseases - False
treatment: Asthma cannot be cured but can be controlled well
Use a quick-relief (reliever) inhaler during an attack
Daily controller inhalers, if prescribed, prevent attacks
Avoid triggers such as smoke, dust and pollution
Get emergency help if breathing is very hard or the reliever inhaler does not help

tuberculosis.vaccine_schedule: BCG at birth; boosters not routinely given.
myths: TB is hereditary - False
Only poor people get TB - False
tuberculosis.outbreak_info: No active outbreak reported in dataset.
treatment: TB is curable with a full course of antibiotics, usually 6 months or more
Free TB treatment is available through government health centres
Never stop medicines early, even if you feel better, as this can cause drug-resistant TB
Cover your mouth when coughing and see a doctor if you have a cough lasting over 2 weeks

malaria.vaccine_schedule: No widely used vaccine for general public; preventive measures recommended.
myths: Only rural areas have malaria - False
malaria.outbreak_info: No active outbreak reported in dataset.
treatment: Malaria is curable with antimalarial medicines after a blood test
Get tested and treated quickly, within 24 hours of fever
Take the full course prescribed by the doctor
Severe malaria with confusion, fits or breathing trouble is an emergency; go to a hospital at once

dengue.vaccine_schedule: No widely used vaccine for general public; preventive measures recommended.
myths: Papaya leaves cure dengue - False
dengue.outbreak_info: No active outbreak reported in dataset.
treatment: There is no specific medicine for dengue; care is supportive
Rest and drink plenty of fluids such as water, ORS and coconut water
Paracetamol can be used for fever; avoid aspirin and ibuprofen as they raise bleeding risk
Go to a hospital at once for severe stomach pain, repeated vomiting, bleeding, black stools, drowsiness or breathing trouble

typhoid.vaccine_schedule: Oral or injectable vaccine recommended for high-risk areas.
myths: Only people with poor hygiene get typhoid - False
typhoid.outbreak_info: No active outbreak reported in dataset.
treatment: Typhoid is treated with antibiotics prescribed by a doctor
Take the full course even if you feel better
Rest and drink plenty of safe fluids and eat light, easily digestible food
Go to a hospital if there is severe stomach pain, confusion or very high fever

hiv aids.vaccine_schedule: No vaccine available; preventive measures recommended.
myths: HIV spreads via casual contact - False
HIV spreads via mosquito bites - False
hiv aids.outbreak_info: No active outbreak reported in dataset.
treatment: There is no cure, but antiretroviral therapy (ART) controls the virus
With regular ART people can live long, healthy lives
ART is available free at government ART centres
People with an undetectable viral load do not pass HIV to partners
Take medicines daily and do not stop without medical advice

myths: Only alcoholics get hepatitis - False
hepatitis b.outbreak_info: No active outbreak reported in dataset.
treatment: Most adults with acute hepatitis B recover with rest, fluids and healthy food
Chronic hepatitis B can be controlled with antiviral medicines under a doctor's care
Avoid alcohol and do not take unprescribed medicines or herbal products
Regular liver checkups are important
The vaccine prevents infection

myths: Flu is always harmless - False
influenza.outbreak_info: No active outbreak reported in dataset.
treatment: Most people recover in about a week with rest and plenty of fluids
Paracetamol can ease fever and body aches
Antiviral medicine may be given by a doctor, especially to high-risk people if started early
Antibiotics do not work on flu
See a doctor if breathing is hard, symptoms get worse, or for children, pregnant women and older adults

diarrhea.vaccine_schedule: Rotavirus vaccine for infants where applicable.
myths: Diarrhea always needs antibiotics - False
diarrhea.outbreak_info: No active outbreak reported in dataset.
treatment: Drink ORS (oral rehydration solution) after every loose stool
Give zinc tablets to children for 10 to 14 days as advised
Keep eating and continue breastfeeding infants
Most cases do not need antibiotics
Go to a doctor if there is blood in stool, high fever, extreme thirst, no urine, or if an infant or older person is affected

myths: All kidney stones need surgery - False
treatment: Treatment aims to slow the damage and protect the kidneys
Control blood pressure and blood sugar and eat less salt
Avoid painkillers such as NSAIDs unless a doctor allows
Take medicines as prescribed and have regular kidney tests
Advanced disease may need dialysis or a kidney transplant
Kidney stones: drink plenty of water; small ones often pass on their own, but see a doctor for severe pain

myths: Only old people get Alzheimer’s - False
Memory loss is normal aging - False
treatment: There is no cure, but treatment can ease symptoms and help daily life
Some medicines may slow memory decline for a time
A regular routine, a safe home and family support help a lot
Keep the person mentally and physically active
Talk to a doctor for the right care plan and caregiver support

corona.vaccine_schedule: Two-dose primary series + boosters as per national guidelines.
myths: COVID-19 is just like flu - False
treatment: Most mild cases recover at home with rest, fluids and isolation
Paracetamol can ease fever and body aches
Seek medical care for breathing difficulty, chest pain, confusion or low oxygen level
Antiviral medicines may be given by a doctor to high-risk patients
Vaccination lowers the risk of severe illness
Rest and drink plenty of fluids
Wear light clothing and use a lukewarm sponge to cool the body
Paracetamol can be used as per label or doctor's advice
See a doctor if fever lasts more than 3 days, is above 103°F (39.4°C), or comes with rash, stiff neck, confusion or breathing trouble
Babies under 3 months with fever need a doctor at once
fever.vaccine_schedule: Not applicable; depends on the cause of the fever.
myths: All fevers indicate serious disease - False
